newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius conglomerate proposes to issue bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius conglomerate proposes to issue bonds.

text.p: Mauritius' largest conglomerate, Rogers, is convening an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on December 16 to approve the public issue of 250 million rupees ($12.5 million) secured bonds, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
Company Secretary Andre Raffray told Reuters that the public issue sought will involve 250,000 bonds with nominal value of 1,000 rupees each.
"The issue will probably be during the first quarter of next year, maybe February," he said.
Raffray said the life duration of the secured bonds was still to be decided by the company's board of directors but will "probably be between 5 and 7 years".
Subject to approval of the bonds public issue, the EGM would also propose a resolution seeking to pledge a floating charge on the company's assets as guarantee for the securities.
Rogers also intends to apply for listing of the bonds on the official market of the Stock Exchange of Mauritius.
